Calibration differs by class: Basal 2.0-max is overconfident in the discrepancy and freshness classes (ECE 0.26 and
0.27) and calibrated in the onboarding class (0.04), where it always chooses an admissible action (escalate in 46 of 60
episodes, a document request in 14) with a mean confidence of 0.96; Liquid AI d1-3B is worst in the discrepancy class
(ECE 0.53: mean confidence 0.84, accuracy 0.35). Liquid AI d1-3B's deferral rule is not monotone: deferring a quarter of
its decisions lowers the unjustified rate to 56\%, deferring half raises it again to 63\%, because its most confident
decisions, in the discrepancy class, are mostly wrong. The confidence of the decision models therefore carries usable
information for triage, but none of the three is calibrated enough for its stated probability to be read as a risk,
which is what a certified threshold rule would need (§6.2).

Table 7 collects these measures; Table 5 reports the calibration of the decision models' confidence and the trade-off of
a confidence-based deferral rule. Out-of-permission actions were attempted by no configuration in any class. Protocol
incidents (all splits): Gemma 4 26B, 13 reseeded retries after rejected tool calls and one run that hit the turn limit;
gpt-oss 120B, one reseeded retry, three decisions recovered from text and one run without a decision; Mistral Small 3.2,
six server timeouts and two runs without a decision; none elsewhere. Excluding the three gpt-oss units with
text-recovered decisions, the robustness check of §5.7, changes no grant, because the configuration certifies nothing in
any class under any rule. Majority voting over the three runs of Claude Haiku 5.5 (all data) certifies the discrepancy
class for the DSA rule (upper bound 0.059 against 0.116 with runs as units), leaves the other grants unchanged and
leaves the delegation-test selections unchanged (both rules delegate the discrepancy class at \(k = 1\) and the
discrepancy and onboarding classes at \(k = 2\)). Escalation calibration varies widely: GPT-6.1 Terra under-escalated
51\% of the onboarding-class arms whose only admissible answer was escalation, and gpt-oss 120B over-escalated 37\% of
the freshness-class arms with an admissible non-escalation answer.
